results.target: The primary composite of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for worsening heart failure, analyzed as time to first event during randomized trial follow-up. Compare assignment to empagliflozin 10 mg once daily versus placebo, each added to recommended therapy, among all randomized patients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction. The intended comparative measure is the hazard ratio; trial follow-up is the window rather than a fixed-duration event risk.
results.outcome: Composite of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for worsening heart failure; time to first event
results.population: All randomized patients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction
results.intervention: Empagliflozin 10 mg once daily plus recommended therapy
results.window: median follow-up 16 months; randomized trial follow-up

assessments.scope_justification: The primary endpoint definition, time-to-first-event approach, assigned treatments and randomized population match the requested target. The estimate is intention-to-treat during trial follow-up, with median follow-up 16 months, rather than a fixed-duration risk.
assessments.population_justification: The primary analysis followed intention to treat and included all randomized participants; 3730 patients with class II-IV HF and LVEF <=40% were randomized.
unknowns: The reported article does not explicitly use the exact phrase HFrEF in this Result; it specifies HF class II-IV and LVEF <=40%.

assessments.scope_justification: The report's primary endpoint is adjudicated cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure, analyzed as time to first event. Assigned arms are empagliflozin 10 mg daily or placebo in addition to recommended/usual HF therapy. The primary analysis is intention-to-treat with Cox proportional hazards. It reports HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.65 to 0.86; P<0.001), median follow-up 16 months.
assessments.population_justification: The report randomized 3730 patients with NYHA class II-IV HF and LVEF <=40%; the primary analysis included all randomized patients. This is the closest supported population to the target's reduced-EF group.
unknowns: The article gives HF with LVEF <=40%, not a separately labeled HFrEF-only definition; target and report are substantively aligned but the terminology is not identical.
Only median follow-up of 16 months is given; individual follow-up window boundaries are not specified.
The abstract's event counts are 361/1863 and 462/1867, and the report notes four placebo-assigned patients did not receive placebo; estimate remains ITT.
